items.title: TSMC October revenue jumps 59.7%; board approves $40.93 billion capacity appropriations
items.summary: TSMC reported record October revenue of NT$586.89 billion, up 59.7% year over year and 14.7% from September. Its board approved $40.93 billion in capital appropriations and up to $500 million each for investments in Anthropic and OpenAI. The approvals are not evidence that funds have been spent or equity purchases closed.

items.title: CoreWeave Q3 revenue jumps 168% and backlog reaches $132.5 billion
items.summary: CoreWeave reported $3.66 billion of Q3 revenue, up 168% year over year, beating estimates, and raised full-year guidance to $13.0–$13.3 billion. Shares rose more than 7% in November 10 extended trading after a severe monthly decline. Its $132.5 billion backlog supports demand visibility, while debt and spending create significant execution risk.

observations.label: Market move
observations.value: More than +7% November 10 after hours; not a confirmed November 11 close

items.key_finding: Strong customer demand contrasts with elevated leverage, capital intensity and backlog conversion risk.

items.title: Reported drone strike causes fire at Russia's Ust-Luga export port
items.summary: Russia's Leningrad governor reported a drone strike and fire at Ust-Luga port, three injured workers and a local power disruption. Ust-Luga handles oil and petroleum-product exports, but the damaged terminal and export-flow impact remain unverified. This is a leading infrastructure-risk signal rather than a confirmed crude-supply outage.

observations.label: Reported physical effect
observations.value: Port-area fire; three injured workers; local power disruption

observations.label: Market price response
observations.value: Not independently established as attributable to this incident

items.key_finding: Ust-Luga port fire warrants monitoring of tanker loading and terminal status, without assuming an oil-flow interruption.

items.title: Oil futures stabilize despite persistent Strait of Hormuz shipping attacks
items.summary: Reuters reported Brent at $92.01 and WTI at $86.20 by 07:30 GMT November 11, modestly above prior two-month lows. A Washington Institute tally cited by Reuters counted 37 vessel attacks in October. Continued attacks are a credible leading risk, but neither a new oil-volume outage nor normalization of transit was verified.

observations.label: Reported October vessel attacks
observations.value: 37 in Hormuz and surrounding waterways; Washington Institute tally cited by Reuters

items.key_finding: Crude stabilization reflects competing diplomatic and security signals, not proof of restored safe shipping.

items.title: Correction: earlier 9.0-million-barrel API crude build alert invalidated
items.summary: An earlier Scout item reported a 9.0-million-barrel US crude inventory build for the week ended November 6. Later OilPrice reporting, a live Trading Economics series and another contemporaneous account instead show a 9.8-million-barrel draw. The earlier build interpretation is invalidated; the competing accounts require verification against the EIA release November 12.

observations.value: November 10, 2026 at 8:27:59 PM EST; reporting reconciliation, not an intraday price confirmation

observations.label: Invalidated previous report
observations.value: API crude inventories +9.0 million barrels for week ending November 6, as reported in prior Scout item

observations.label: Newer reported API crude figure
observations.value: -9.8 million barrels, i.e. draw rather than build; provisional industry estimate

observations.label: Price reaction
observations.value: Not independently established after the publication of these API figures

observations.label: Official EIA check
observations.value: November 12, 2026 at 12:00 PM EST (Veterans Day schedule); not yet released

items.key_finding: Material source contradiction reverses the earlier API crude-build interpretation; treat the original Scout alert as invalid pending official reconciliation.
